probe: correct translation, timing preserved
transcript: Give ah ma her medicine after dinner.
draft_translation: Please give grandmother her medicine after dinner.
watch_for: baseline case -- if this fails, the verifier is too strict, not too lenient.

probe: timing silently flipped in translation
transcript: Give ah ma her medicine after dinner.
draft_translation: Please give grandmother her medicine before dinner.
watch_for: if verdict comes back PASS, the verifier is only checking fluency, not meaning -- this is the single most important case in the set.

probe: correct translation, negation preserved
transcript: Close the window, it's cold.
draft_translation: Please close the window, it is cold.

probe: negation dropped in translation
transcript: Don't close the window, I want fresh air.
draft_translation: Please close the window, I want fresh air.
watch_for: a dropped negation flips the instruction's meaning entirely -- this is the highest-stakes error type for caregiving.

probe: Singlish urgency preserved correctly
transcript: Wa lau, jio ah ma makan already lah, don't delay.
draft_translation: Please call grandmother to eat now, don't delay.

probe: urgency softened away in translation
transcript: Wa lau, jio ah ma makan already lah, don't delay.
draft_translation: Whenever convenient, you could call grandmother to eat.
watch_for: urgency loss is subtle -- the sentence still reads as fluent, plausible English. Checks the verifier isn't just fluency-scoring.

probe: TCM-adjacent phrase, correctly translated as soreness
transcript: Ah gong cannot makan too much sio bak, doctor said.

interpretation.action: should not eat too much roast pork

draft_translation: Grandfather should not eat too much roast pork, the doctor said.

probe: context-resolved object correctly carried through
transcript: Bring that one to her room, she asked for it earlier.
draft_translation: Please bring the shawl to her room, she asked for it earlier.

probe: resolved object swapped for a different one in translation
transcript: Bring that one to her room, she asked for it earlier.
draft_translation: Please bring the blanket to her room, she asked for it earlier.
watch_for: the interpretation already resolved the reference correctly -- this tests whether verify catches the TRANSLATION step losing it, not the interpretation step.

probe: unresolved referent should route to clarify, not retry
transcript: Put that one back where it was.

interpretation.object: unresolved - no prior reference in context

draft_translation: Please put it back where it was.
watch_for: translation is a faithful rendering of an already-ambiguous interpretation -- retrying translation cannot fix this. If verdict is RETRY, fault_source classification is not working.

probe: vague timing at the source, not a translation problem
transcript: Do it later, not now, but also not too late.

interpretation.timing: vague - later but before an unspecified deadline

draft_translation: Please do it at some point later.
watch_for: this is the case that most directly tests whether the retry cap is being spent wisely -- a RETRY here would burn the team's one retry on an unfixable problem.

probe: multi-element instruction, all preserved
transcript: Don't give her the hot soup before 6pm, wait for the medicine first, then after 30 minutes give the soup.
draft_translation: Please do not give her the hot soup before 6pm. Give the medicine first, then wait 30 minutes before giving the soup.

probe: multi-element instruction, negation and sequence both dropped
transcript: Don't give her the hot soup before 6pm, wait for the medicine first, then after 30 minutes give the soup.
draft_translation: Please give her the hot soup before 6pm, then give the medicine.
watch_for: two elements broken at once (negation + sequence) -- checks the verifier doesn't stop looking after finding one issue.

probe: conditional urgency, correctly translated
transcript: If she says her chest hurts, stop everything and call me immediately, don't wait.
draft_translation: If she says her chest hurts, stop everything and call me right away, do not wait.
watch_for: highest real-world stakes case in the set -- a false PASS here is the worst possible failure mode for the whole product.

probe: conditional urgency dropped -- most safety-critical injected error
transcript: If she says her chest hurts, stop everything and call me immediately, don't wait.
draft_translation: If she mentions chest discomfort, you can call me sometime after.
watch_for: if this one is ever missed, it goes straight into the demo as the strongest justification for having a verifier at all.

probe: correct object preserved, simple case
transcript: Fetch her glasses from the drawer.
draft_translation: Please fetch her glasses from the drawer.

probe: object swapped for something plausible but wrong
transcript: Fetch her glasses from the drawer.
draft_translation: Please fetch her gloves from the drawer.
watch_for: single-word substitution, plausible in isolation -- checks the verifier is cross-referencing the interpretation, not just judging fluency.

probe: TCM-adjacent phrase correctly kept as non-clinical
transcript: Eat too much fried food, she said she feels 热气.
draft_translation: She said she feels heaty after eating too much fried food.

probe: TCM idiom escalated into an invented clinical finding
transcript: Eat too much fried food, she said she feels 热气.
draft_translation: She said she has a fever after eating too much fried food.
watch_for: translation invents a clinical symptom (fever) that was never in the interpretation -- checks the verifier catches fabrication, not just omission.

probe: context-resolved pronoun correctly carried through
transcript: That one is due already.
draft_translation: The diaper is due to be changed now.

probe: correctly resolved object dropped entirely in translation
transcript: That one is due already.
draft_translation: It's about time now.
watch_for: an omission error, not a substitution -- the object vanishes rather than being swapped. Checks the verifier catches missing information, not just wrong information.

probe: vague quantity at the source -- second source-ambiguity stress test
transcript: Just give her some water, not too much.
draft_translation: Please give her some water, not too much.
watch_for: reclassified from CLARIFY to PASS -- 'not too much' is imprecise but actionable caregiving language, not a blocking ambiguity like an unresolved referent (v010/v030) or an undefined deadline (v011). If this starts failing, check whether the prompt has become too aggressive about flagging any imprecise quantity as source_ambiguity.

probe: vague-sounding timing that recent_context actually resolves
transcript: Do it soon.

interpretation.object: 8am tablet (resolved via recent_context: 'her tablet is on the counter')
interpretation.timing: resolved to right after breakfast, per household routine in recent_context

draft_translation: Please give her the tablet right after breakfast, as usual.
watch_for: looks superficially like v011/v022 (vague-sounding transcript) but the interpretation has ALREADY resolved it via context. Checks the verifier isn't pattern-matching on 'vague-sounding transcript' but actually reading the interpretation it was given.

probe: multi-step sequence, second variant, all preserved
transcript: First check her temperature, if it's normal then help her get dressed, if not call me.

interpretation.action: check temperature, then conditionally dress or call

draft_translation: Please check her temperature first. If it's normal, help her get dressed. If not, call me.
watch_for: structurally similar to v012 (which failed) -- run this one first when investigating whether the model has a general weakness with multi-branch instructions or if v012 specifically was a fluke.

probe: multi-step sequence, second variant, one branch dropped
transcript: First check her temperature, if it's normal then help her get dressed, if not call me.

interpretation.action: check temperature, then conditionally dress or call

draft_translation: Please check her temperature, then help her get dressed.
watch_for: drops the entire conditional call-for-help branch -- a safety-relevant omission, not just an inaccuracy.

probe: dosage quantity correctly preserved
transcript: Give her two tablets, not three, the doctor changed the dose.
draft_translation: Please give her two tablets, not three -- the doctor changed the dose.
watch_for: dosage errors are the single highest-consequence category for this product -- worth having more than one case here as the eval set grows further.

probe: dosage quantity swapped -- highest real-world stakes injected error
transcript: Give her two tablets, not three, the doctor changed the dose.
draft_translation: Please give her three tablets, as the doctor said.
watch_for: a single swapped number, otherwise fluent and plausible -- if this is ever missed, it is a more serious real-world failure than any other case in this set.

probe: conditional safety instruction, second variant, correctly preserved
transcript: If she can't stand up on her own, don't force it, just call for help.

interpretation.action: do not force standing, call for help instead

draft_translation: If she cannot stand up on her own, do not force her, just call for help.

probe: conditional safety instruction, negation and urgency both flattened
transcript: If she can't stand up on her own, don't force it, just call for help.

interpretation.action: do not force standing, call for help instead

draft_translation: If she has trouble standing, you could try helping her up.
watch_for: the negation ('don't force it') is inverted into its opposite ('try helping her up') -- this is the same failure category as v004 but at higher real-world stakes.

probe: ambiguous pronoun with two plausible referents in context, genuinely unresolved
transcript: Give it to him when he wakes up.

interpretation.object: unresolved - recent_context mentions both 'his medicine' and 'his glasses' with no clear antecedent for 'it'

draft_translation: Please give it to him when he wakes up.
watch_for: third source-ambiguity case, deliberately using a different flavour of ambiguity (competing referents, not vague timing/quantity) than v011/v022 -- if the model handles one flavour but not another, that's useful prompt-tuning information.

probe: clear transcript, interpretation contradicts it directly, translation faithfully reflects the wrong interpretation
transcript: Give her the red pill, not the blue one.
draft_translation: Please give her the blue pill.
watch_for: the transcript is completely unambiguous ('red, not blue') -- this is not a vague source, it's a clean misread by the interpretation step. Translation faithfully carries the error forward, so the draft is not itself at fault.

probe: clear transcript, negation/timing swapped in interpretation despite explicit statement
transcript: Ah ma's appointment is at 3pm today, not tomorrow.
draft_translation: Grandmother's appointment is tomorrow at 3pm.
watch_for: the transcript explicitly negates 'tomorrow' -- there is nothing vague here, so this must not be classified as source_ambiguity. Distinguishes a genuine misread from genuine vagueness.

probe: boundary case: same surface shape as v032, but the source really is vague this time
transcript: The appointment got moved, not sure exactly when now.

interpretation.timing: unresolved - transcript itself does not state a new time

draft_translation: The appointment has been moved to a new time.
watch_for: run this alongside v032 whenever tuning the prompt -- v032 has a clear source with a wrong interpretation (should be 'interpretation'), this one has a genuinely vague source (should be 'source_ambiguity'). If the model confuses these two, the three-way distinction is not landing.

probe: correct interpretation and correct translation of an unambiguous transcript -- control case for the new category
transcript: Give her the red pill, not the blue one.
draft_translation: Please give her the red pill, not the blue one.
watch_for: same transcript as v031, correct interpretation and translation this time -- checks the new interpretation-fault logic doesn't make the model over-suspicious of interpretations in general.
